entities.summary:
Philippe de Lévis (1435–1475) was a French Roman Catholic bishop and cardinal.

A prominent figure in the Catholic Church during the late 15th century, Philippe de Lévis played a significant role in the papal elections of 1464 and 1471. He was a key advisor to Pope Pius II and participated in the Council of Basel, where he contributed to the development of the Conciliar movement.

As a cardinal, Philippe de Lévis was instrumental in shaping the policies of the Catholic Church during this period. He was a strong supporter of the Counter-Reformation and worked closely with other prominent clergy to counter the spread of Protestantism.

Despite his significant contributions to the Catholic Church, Philippe de Lévis's legacy has been somewhat overshadowed by that of other prominent figures from this era. Nevertheless, his work continues to be studied by historians and scholars seeking to understand the complexities of the Catholic Church during the late Middle Ages.

The phrase 'in loco parentis' – 'in the place of a parent' – is often attributed to Philippe de Lévis, reflecting his role as a guardian and protector of the Catholic Church's interests.
